blindSummary:
This state/province is one of twelve in the country applying religious criminal law in parallel with the federal system since the 2002 wave. The religious penal code criminalises same-sex acts between men and between women for adherents of the state religion, with penalties reaching beyond the federal fourteen-year prohibition-law term. No trans-specific incident, religious morality-police activity, or international-commission case documentation is on record for this state/province. The legal framework itself is the finding; the absence of documented enforcement is a reporting-decay limitation (an assessment body states its figures represent only a fraction of the true scale), not evidence of safety.

Within the country's religious-law states this state/province sits with a seven-state bloc whose defining feature is an enacted, capital-capable criminal law and a parallel court jurisdiction, but without the documented morality-police enforcement layer or case-level evidence that worsens the position of five other religious-law states/provinces.
